newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may revise ownership rules for CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may revise ownership rules for CVRD.

text.p: Brazil is likely to revise some of the sell-off rules for state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) to prevent single buyers taking control, Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito told a newspaper.

Brito told Wednesday's Correio Braziliense daily he wanted to prevent large iron ore producers, consumers and traders from using front companies or subsidiaries to circumvent limits set on how large a share they can buy of CVRD.
He also said the government might allow staff to participate in an initial block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares slated to go on the auction block next February.

Under rules agreed in September for the auction of the block share, iron ore producers of over 30 million tonnes, consumers of over 8.0 million tonnes and traders of over 30 million tonnes a year will be restricted to a maximum 45 percent of the block.
No individual producer, consumer or trader falling within those categories may own more than 10 percent of the block.

Brito said the government had realized these firms could use subsidiaries or front companies to circumvent the limit. "All of the errors, loopholes or lack of detail will be corrected in the tender details, which will be published in December," Correio quoted him as saying.
Under the original sell-off plans, 10 percent of voting shares will be offered to staff after the initial block sale.
Brito said the government had not yet decided whether to let employees participate in the block sale or to allow them to benefit from any possible subsequent mark-up in share value.
The government owns 76 percent of CVRD's voting capital, equivalent to 51 percent of the company's total capital.
After the block sale and the sale to employees, Brazil intends to float the rest of its holding on domestic and international markets through a public offering.
